summary.text: Maura Keller is a retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel with 26 years of service and a later career as a defense personnel consultant and nuclear medicine technologist at the Atlanta VA. She is the Democratic nominee for Georgia's 3rd Congressional District, having also been the party's nominee in 2024, and describes her campaign as focused on raising the minimum wage and economic opportunity.

paragraphs.text: Born in Weymouth, Massachusetts (she describes it as South Weymouth) and attended Weymouth South High School; she says she has lived in Fayetteville, Georgia, for 30 years.
Enlisted in the U.S. Army in 1978 as a military police soldier, was later commissioned as an officer, and retired as a lieutenant colonel after 26 years; Ballotpedia lists her service as 1978-2004.
Earned bachelor's degrees from Excelsior College (1994) and Augusta University (2017), and a military citation from the Command and General Staff College at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas (1997).

In retirement, she says she worked as a senior consultant in military personnel and readiness, providing analytical support to the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness and the Chief, Army Reserve.
Earned a degree in Radiologic Sciences (Nuclear Medicine Technology) and, by her own account, worked at the Atlanta VA supporting veterans.
Describes receiving the General Douglas MacArthur Leadership Award among her military honors.
Was the Democratic nominee in 2024, losing to Brian Jack 33.7% to 66.3%; won the 2026 Democratic primary on May 19, 2026, with 60.8% over George Melville Johnson.
